text:
maya: heads-up, ran a 8xA100 TP+PP smoke and saw a 15-30% tail latency increase on stage 2 all-reduces vs last week. low-msgs path looks bad.
samir: ugh. any idea ring vs tree behavior? we recently toggled redispatch heuristics.
maya: initial flamegraphs point to long NCCL_Wait and repeated tiny sends. looks like handshakes/backpressure causing extra rendezvous.
liam: can you paste the perf counters? also which kernel selector was used (fp16/qat/int8)?
maya: profiling snippet:
```
NCCL_ALLREDUCE: calls=1200, avg_bytes=2300, p50=1.9ms, p95=8.7ms
cudaKernel(softmax): avg=0.8ms
cudaMemcpyAsync: intermittent 3-6ms spikes
NVLINK_P2P: 3.2% time
```
maya: interestingly the runtime flipped to the tree path for ~30% of rounds when msgsize < 4k, redispatch log shows `switch_to_tree` at handshake
julia: that flip is new since the adaptive-redispatch patch last deploy. it tries to avoid ring tail on microbursts but might be thrashing.
samir: KV cache could be changing message boundaries: prefix hits shorten next request, creating varying msg sizes that cross the heuristic threshold.
liam: so we have two interacting flows: batching heuristic + kv cache variability -> message-size jitter -> redispatch churn -> handshake/backpressure -> NCCL stalls
maya: repro command i used:
```
PYTHONPATH=. python tools/bench_tp_allreduce.py --topo tp4_pp2 --batch 12 --seq-len 512 --msgs 1200 --kv-cache True
```
maya: attaching short perf trace link: https://ci.internal/redwood/trace/3712345678 (dev-bot posted)
dev-bot: [automated] trace uploaded: https://ci.internal/redwood/trace/3712345678
julia: quick mitigations we can try:
- increase msgsize threshold for switching to tree (e.g. 4k->8k)
- add hysteresis to redispatch (require N consecutive rounds before flip)
- disable redispatch for configs with kv-cache enabled
- add a prefix-coalesce in batching to stabilize sizes
samir: agree. also add logging to kernel-selector to record why fp16->int8 switch happened; kernel switch during handshake could be expensive.
liam: i can run the hysteresis patch locally and re-run maya's repro. if it helps we can roll a canary tomorrow.
maya: one more note: nsight timeline shows pipeline gaps aligned to handshake times, not compute. that means comm/compute overlap is being lost during the flip.
julia: capture action items:
1) liam: try hysteresis + run the bench by EOD (linux/gpu-qa)
2) samir: add kernel-selector debug logs + flag to disable autoswitch
3) maya: collect a few more traces with and without kv-cache on same model
4) julia: draft a short rollback plan for redispatch patch if canary regresses
liam: ack, will report back.
maya: thanks — keeping this in thread for traceability :thumbsup:
